saints.name: St. Vincent of Saragossa
saints.title: Deacon and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: A deacon of Spain whose endurance under fearful tortures made him one of the most honored martyrs of the West…
biography: Vincent was born at Huesca in Spain and ordained deacon by Valerius, bishop of Saragossa, whose spokesman he became, for the bishop stammered. In the persecution of Diocletian both were brought before Dacian, the governor, at Valencia, and Vincent answered for the Church that they were ready to suffer all things rather than surrender the Scriptures to the fire.

The enraged judge put Vincent to every torture: the rack, iron hooks, salt rubbed into his wounds, and a red-hot gridiron, then a dungeon floor strewn with broken potsherds, where he died in 304. His serenity shook his own jailer, who was converted, and his body, cast into the sea, was thrown back ashore and honorably buried at Valencia.

Prudentius crowned him in verse within the century, and Augustine, preaching on his feast, noted that his fame reached wherever the name of Christ was known; in 1173 King Afonso I of Portugal brought his relics by sea to Lisbon, whose arms still show the ship and the ravens. Deacon and patron of deacons, he is patron also of vintners, his very name being heard in the French vin.
